questions: Do line_loss_events reach 0 on all three development tracks with the ±6 cm array?
If the robot still goes off track, is max_error near 0.06 m on a bend, and at what progress?
With weights scaled to x/0.03 (so the maximum weight is ±2), is the controller's kp and kd scale workable, or does the signal saturate?
Does steering_oscillation stay near the baseline of 0.07-0.15, or does the larger array or the 3 cm lead raise it?
Does the 0.10 m track turn fast enough to get completion_time under 3.0 s?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line losses are 0 but the robot still leaves the track, tell me whether a shorter lead (0.02 m) or a larger sensor_size would help more. If the signal is too weak with a 6 cm span, say so and I will narrow the span to ±5 cm.

intent: Test whether a wide seven-sensor array (±6 cm, 2 cm pitch, 16 mm footprints) at a 3 cm lead keeps the line under the sensors through bends, so that line losses reach 0 and the robot stops leaving the track at about 11-16% progress. The narrower wheel track should help it turn. Expect line_loss_events near 0, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress well above 0.15. If it still goes off track with no line losses, the next change is the lead or the gains.
learning: Evidence so far: iteration 0 (±2 cm span, 5 cm lead, 0.8 kg, 0.12 m track) gave 1-2 line losses and off-track at 10-15% progress on all runs. Iteration 1 (±3 cm span, 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track) reduced losses to 1 per run but still went off track at 11-16% progress. Body width has no effect within range because the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m. Measurements to check next: completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error, rms_error, steering_oscillation and control_effort on every development track.
rationale: Iteration 1 (0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 4 cm lead, ±3 cm span) was only a small improvement: line losses fell from 1-2 to 1 per run, but all 60 runs still went off track at 11-16% progress, with max_error of 0.061-0.066 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). At body_width 0.12 that is 0.06 m, and no allowed body width raises it above 0.06 m (0.18 m gives 0.0575 m), so body width cannot widen the margin. The robot is therefore drifting about 6 cm from the line, and the sensors do not hold it there. The span is the main limit: ±3 cm covers only about ±4.5 cm of tape-centre offset with 12 mm footprints, so a bend pushes the line out from under the array. I will widen the span to ±6 cm with seven sensors at 2 cm pitch, which is the maximum sensor count and wider than any observed excursion. I will use 16 mm footprints so neighbouring sensors overlap and at least one covers the 25 mm tape at every offset in the span. The lead moves to 3 cm, as the Integrator requested, to read bends earlier. Wheel track drops to 0.10 m to turn more readily, and mass stays at 0.6 kg. Expected result: line_loss_events near 0, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress well above 0.15. If the robot still leaves at low line loss, the forward offset or gains are the limit, not the span.
